context: bro actually finished the whole pizza no cap
target_audience: parent trying to understand their teenager
criteria: correctly defines as 'not lying' or 'for real'
does not confuse with a physical cap or hat
gives a natural rephrasing of the example sentence
tone is helpful not condescending

context: he just started reorganising the entire office layout by himself — what the sigma
target_audience: colleague who saw it in a work group chat
criteria: explains it is a gen alpha replacement for 'what the hell' or 'what on earth'
conveys it expresses surprise or bewilderment, not necessarily negative
notes it is a deliberate meme substitution of a swear word
does not attempt to explain sigma as a personality type in this context

context: he doesn't care what anyone thinks, just locks in and gets it done — total sigma
target_audience: manager trying to understand why their team keeps calling a quiet colleague this
criteria: explains sigma as self-sufficient, independent, and unbothered by social validation
distinguishes it from alpha — sigma is not about dominance but indifference to the hierarchy entirely
correctly reads the context as a compliment
does not reduce it to just introvert — quiet confidence and competence must come through

context: my little brother watches skibidi toilet for hours, what even is that
target_audience: older sibling or parent with no context
criteria: explains it is a YouTube/internet series featuring toilets with human heads
conveys it is intentionally absurd and the appeal is the absurdity itself
does not try to assign deeper meaning where there is none
reassures the reader it is harmless internet humour popular with younger kids

context: she walked into the pitch and just mogged the entire room without saying a word
target_audience: recruiter who saw it in a candidate review
criteria: defines mogging as effortlessly outshining or overshadowing others
conveys it is used admiringly not aggressively
correctly reads this as a compliment about commanding presence
does not require knowledge of any prior internet subculture to understand

context: he walked in and immediately had the whole room — man's got rizz
target_audience: general adult unfamiliar with gen alpha slang
criteria: defines as natural charisma or ability to attract others effortlessly
explains it can be used as a noun or verb
does not reduce it to just physical attractiveness
example usage in explanation is natural and accurate

context: that presentation slide is giving 2009 PowerPoint
target_audience: designer colleague who hasn't heard the phrase
criteria: explains it means something strongly evokes or resembles something else
captures that it can be used positively or critically depending on context
correctly reads this example as mildly critical
does not over-explain or add unnecessary cultural history

context: stop being such an NPC and make your own decisions for once
target_audience: manager who heard it used about a colleague
criteria: explains NPC stands for non-playable character from video games
correctly defines it here as calling someone passive or lacking independent thought
notes it is being used as a mild insult in this context
does not require gaming knowledge from the reader to understand the explanation

context: she showed up to the costume party in full armour — she understood the assignment
target_audience: HR manager who saw it in a Slack channel
criteria: explains it means someone fully committed to what was expected and delivered perfectly
conveys it is a strong compliment
clarifies it is not literally about an assignment or homework
gives a workplace-appropriate equivalent phrase

context: her keynote speech? she ate and left no crumbs
target_audience: colleague who read it in a post-event debrief
criteria: explains it means someone performed exceptionally and flawlessly
makes clear it has nothing to do with food
conveys strong admiration
accurately rephrases the example in plain english

context: you've been arguing about this game for six hours straight, go touch grass
target_audience: parent who saw it in their child's group chat
criteria: explains it means go outside or take a break from screens
conveys it is used as mild mockery or friendly advice
correctly reads the context as telling someone to step away and get perspective
does not interpret it as threatening or seriously rude

context: she walked into the interview like she already had the job — total main character energy
criteria: explains it means behaving as if you are the confident protagonist of your own story
conveys it is generally used as a compliment meaning self-assured and decisive
does not conflate it with arrogance or self-absorption
correctly reads the interview example as a positive observation

context: she genuinely thinks she's getting promoted after three months — she's so delulu
target_audience: friend group chat observer who doesn't know the word
criteria: explains delulu is a playful shortening of delusional
conveys it is used to describe someone with unrealistic expectations or hopes
captures that it is often used affectionately or with light mockery rather than as a serious insult
correctly reads the context as gently mocking the person's optimism
notes the word can also be used self-deprecatingly as in 'i know i'm being delulu but'

context: she walked out in that outfit and absolutely slayed
target_audience: parent who heard their teenager say it about a celebrity
criteria: explains slay means to perform, look, or do something impressively and confidently
conveys it is an enthusiastic compliment
notes it has roots in LGBTQ+ and ballroom culture before entering mainstream gen alpha usage
does not over-explain the cultural history at the expense of the simple definition
correctly reads the example as a style or confidence compliment

context: exams are next week, it's time to lock in
target_audience: teacher who keeps hearing students say this before revision season
criteria: explains lock in means to focus completely, eliminate distractions, and commit to a task
conveys it carries a tone of serious intentional effort — more intense than just 'concentrate'
correctly reads the academic context as motivational not negative
notes it can be used as self-directed encouragement or directed at others
does not confuse with the literal meaning of being locked inside somewhere
